images.caption: Figure 1:FilmBench evaluation taxonomy: 3 L1 axes, 12 L2 components, 35+3 (R2V-only) L3 sub-metrics, built from clips across 20 film genres curated by expert directors.

Figure 2:The director-driven reverse-engineering pipeline that turns
award-winning film clips into film-grade prompts; see
§3.1for details.

Figure 3:Fine-grained, per-dimension FilmBench evaluation on a multi-shot
reference-scene (R2V) example reverse-engineered fromLa La Land:
Seedance 2.0 (94.97) vs. Vidu Q2 Pro (73.61). Discussed in the text.

Figure 4:Multi-shot T2V example (a sci-fi mech battle): Seedance 2.0
(86.11) vs. Grok Imagine Video (55.97). Discussed in the text.

Figure 5:Overall FilmBench scores (0–100) per model; model names are printed
inside each bar and the dashed line is the cross-model average. Left: T2V
(N=515N=515); right: R2V (N=654N=654).

Figure 6:Cross-model variance per L3 sub-metric (main bars, colored by
axis), with L2 inset (upper right), computed over the merged T2V+R2V model
means (Hailuo excluded).

Figure 7:Per-axis rankings for T2V (left, 9 models) and R2V (right, 7 models).
Each model is scored on three L1 axes: Instruction Following (solid),
Temporal Continuity (hatched), and Aesthetic Quality (dotted). Models are
ranked by overall score; R2V Instruction Following includes the visual-following
component.

Figure 8:Per-model rankings within the L2 components most related to
audiovisual language:Cinematic Language(solid, centre, model names
inside; also the sort key), flanked byScene(hatched) andCharacter & performance(dotted). T2V (left, 9 models) and R2V
(right, 7 models). The full L2 rankings are in the appendix.

Figure 9:Per-model rankings for the three highest-variance L3 sub-metrics
(computed over merged T2V+R2V data):Camera movement(hatched),Focus(solid, model names inside), andShot scale(dotted).
T2V (left, 9 models) and R2V (right, 7 models).
The full per-metric panels are in the appendix.

left: T2V (n=243n=243/272272), right: R2V (n=239n=239/415415).

Figure 11:Overall score heatmap across the top 4 genres by sample size. Y-axis: genres (with sample sizes T2V/R2V); X-axis: models split into T2V (left) and R2V (right) sections. Each cell shows the genre-specific mean score.

Figure 14:R2V visual-following (reference-fidelity) ranking by reference type
(columns: scene / prop / character).

Figure 15:Cinematic Language L3 sub-metric cross-model means (0–100), T2V
(hatched) vs. R2V (solid), sorted by descending score. Bars are colored by
L2 group: Cinematic Language (blue), editing (red), performance (purple).

Figure 16:R2V reference-character example in 3D animation: Seedance 2.0 (85.43) vs. Grok Imagine Video (63.57). Character-appearance fidelity is high, but the score gap is driven by Cinematic Language and character performance.

Figure 17:R2V reference-prop example in 3D animation: Seedance 2.0 (82.75) vs. Kling 3.0 Omni (79.36). Both score 0 on prop-reference fidelity because the prop’s color is altered by a golden energy aura intended for
the character; the overall gap is again driven by Cinematic Language.
